name: walmsley2024_milk_evaporator
description: Two-effect MVR milk evaporator with milk heat treatment, 247 t/h raw milk (30 t/h milk powder); evaporation system in isolation. Loads in kW.
reference: Walmsley, Lincoln, Padullés, Cleland (2024), Energies 17, 2838, Table 2.

provenance.stream data: published (Table 2); Table 2 dT_cont used (chiller water 0.5 K; the text's pinch range implies 2.5 K, which leaves the targets unchanged)
provenance.eta_lorenz: published: 50 % exergetic (Carnot) efficiency (Sec. 4.2); reproduces the paper's simple-design COP 2.1
provenance.source_T_C: published: ambient / dead state 15 °C (Sec. 2), the source of the paper's simple design
provenance.sink levels: 105 °C published (simple design, Sec. 4.2.3); the 15-55 °C level is assumed (illustrative, follows the low-temperature part of the GCC)
provenance.economics: assumed: no economic data in the source (see economics.sources)
provenance.film coefficients: Stampfli et al. (2018) dairy values, stream mapping assumed

economics._note: No economic data in the source. Prices: Eurostat Portugal 2026-S1 for the consumption band at 8000 h/year; heat pump investment: Danish Energy Agency catalogue by sink temperature (≤60, ≤125, ≤150 °C); other parameters: tool defaults (Sources page). All are assumptions for this case.

hp_dea_1_1.source: Danish Energy Agency, Technology Data - Industrial Process Heat (2025), 'Nominal investment (*total)' 2025, equipment + installation, per MW of heat output, sheet 1.1 'Heat pump, up to 60 °C, temp. lift 40 K': 0.95 M€/MW (0.91-0.95), unit size 0.5-5 MW

hp_dea_2a.source: Danish Energy Agency, Technology Data - Industrial Process Heat (2025), 'Nominal investment (*total)' 2025, equipment + installation, per MW of heat output, sheet 2.a 'High-temperature heat pumps up to 125 °C': 1.2 M€/MW (0.9-1.5), unit size 0.3-25 MW

hp_dea_2b.source: Danish Energy Agency, Technology Data - Industrial Process Heat (2025), 'Nominal investment (*total)' 2025, equipment + installation, per MW of heat output, sheet 2.b 'High-temperature heat pumps up to 150 °C': 1.55 M€/MW (1.25-1.8), unit size 0.5-80 MW. No catalogue sheet above 150 °C: units with hotter sinks are costed with this sheet as an extrapolation (flagged)

sources.prices: Eurostat nrg_pc_203 (gas) and nrg_pc_205 (electricity), Portugal, 2026-S1, excluding VAT and other recoverable taxes and levies, EUR/kWh, gas on GCV (data/sources/eurostat_portugal_prices.csv). The source plant is not in Portugal: these prices place it in the dissertation's Portuguese context. Bands at 8000 h/year: gas 120,700 GJ/year (I4); heat pump electricity 11,700 MWh/year (ID; site total unknown). Bands change with the hours: gas I3 (10,000-99,999 GJ) = 0.0512, I4 (100,000-999,999 GJ) = 0.0445; electricity ID (2,000-19,999 MWh) = 0.1135, IE (20,000-69,999 MWh) = 0.0897
sources.heat_pump_cost: Danish Energy Agency catalogue (2025) by sink temperature, linear in capacity (see cost_functions); replaces Padullés et al. (2026, Table 3), which is fitted to brewery heat pumps and gives 0.75-0.88 M€/MW for 2-3 MW units, below the catalogue range 0.9-1.5 M€/MW for sinks up to 125 °C. Indirect costs (new hot-water piping, 0.19-0.23 M€/MW) not included

area_targeting.film_coefficients_source: Stampfli et al. (2018), CET 70, 901-906, Table 1 (dairy plant): liquid product 500, water 2,000, evaporation/condensation 5,000 W/(m2 K). Mapping to these streams is our assumption: water for chiller water, CIP, direct-use water and cow water (milk condensate); product for raw milk and concentrate; condensation for vapour bleed, condenser and flash vapours

cost_law.label: Towler 2020 plate and frame (304 SS), bare (F = 1)
cost_law.source: Sinnott and Towler (2020), Table 6.6, plate and frame (304 SS), Ce = 1,350 + 180 S^0.95 USD (USGC, Jan 2007, CEPCI 509.7), valid 1-500 m2; x CEPCI 797.9/509.7 (2023; Chem. Eng. Sept 2024 p. 45) / 1.0816 USD/EUR (ECB, 2023)

cost_law.label: Towler 2020 plate and frame (304 SS) x 3.5 (Hand factor, installed)
cost_law.source: Sinnott and Towler (2020), Table 6.6, plate and frame (304 SS), Ce = 1,350 + 180 S^0.95 USD (USGC, Jan 2007, CEPCI 509.7), valid 1-500 m2; x CEPCI 797.9/509.7 (2023; Chem. Eng. Sept 2024 p. 45) / 1.0816 USD/EUR (ECB, 2023); x 3.5 Hand installation factor for heat exchangers (Table 6.3)

area_targeting._cold_utility: cold utility cost not included (no source for this site): TAC is a lower bound below the pinch

basis_hint: No operating hours are published for this plant. Milk supply varies considerably during the year (Atkins et al., 2009, PRES conference), so New Zealand milk-powder plants do not run all year: 8000 h/year is an upper bound. Test lower values; the gas price band also changes (Sources page).
